title.value: Protective effectiveness of previous SARS-CoV-2 infection and hybrid immunity against the omicron variant and severe disease: a systematic review and meta-regression
title.justification: The title was chosen directly from the paper, which is typical for academic articles.
title.quote: Protective effectiveness of previous SARS-CoV-2 infection and hybrid immunity against the omicron variant and severe disease: a systematic review and meta-regression

extractions.description: This paper conducts a systematic review and meta-regression analysis to evaluate the protective effectiveness and durability of previous SARS-CoV-2 infection and hybrid immunity (combination of prior infection and vaccination) against the Omicron variant and severe COVID-19. It highlights the higher and more sustained protection conferred by hybrid immunity compared to vaccination alone. The study aims to guide vaccination strategies by examining the magnitude and duration of protection against reinfection and severe outcomes.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is on evaluating the effectiveness of COVID-19 immunity strategies rather than directly addressing climate or ecological sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Background The global surge in the omicron (B.1.1.529) variant has resulted in many individuals with hybrid immunity (immunity developed through a combination of SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination).

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily concerns medical and public health considerations related to COVID-19 immunity, which does not align directly with climate or ecological sustainable development categories.
primary_category.quote: Restricting the spread of SARS-CoV-2 infection and preventing severe COVID-19 remains a priority at the global scale.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not fit into any sub-category of climate or ecological sustainable development as it focuses on epidemiological and public health research.
primary_sub_category.quote: This systematic review and meta-regression found that both previous infection alone and previous infection combined with previous vaccination (ie, hybrid immunity) conferred rapidly waning protection against SARS-CoV-2 infection with the omicron variant, but high and sustained protection against hospital admission or severe disease due to the omicron variant.

new_primary_category.justification: No new category needs to be suggested as the paper does not directly relate to climate or ecological sustainable development.
new_primary_category.quote: At the public health level, these findings can be combined with data on local infection prevalence, vaccination rates, and their timing.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category is required for this paper, as it does not align with ecological or climate sustainability themes.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our findings make clear the substantial durability of hybrid immunity and could help inform the timing and prioritisation of vaccination programmes in populations with high rates of past infection.
